We have mass spectrum data. Need to identify elements definitively based on isotope distribution patterns visible. Look at peaks: m/z values around 232-240. Likely isotopic pattern of chlorine? Cl has 35Cl (75.78%) at 34.969, 37Cl (24.22%) at 36.966. Not matching. Bromine 79/81 ~ 1:1, masses ~78.9183 and 80.9163. Not match. Sulfur isotopes: 32S 95%, 33S 0.75% at +1, 34S 4.2% +2, 36S 0.02% +4. Not match.

Carbon isotopic pattern: 12C vs 13C difference 1.00335. For large molecules, isotopic envelope spaced by ~1.003. Here peaks spaced ~1.003? Let's compute differences: 231.96544 to 232.96883 diff ~1.00339. Next 233.96320 diff ~0.99437? Actually 232.96883 to 233.96320 diff ~0.99437 (close to 1). Next 233.96320 to 234.96657 diff ~1.00337. Next 234.96657 to 235.96061 diff ~0.9940. So pattern of ~1 Da spacing suggests carbon isotopic pattern (13C). Also presence of peaks at +2, +3 etc. So carbon definitely present.

Other elements with characteristic isotopic patterns: chlorine (35/37 ~2 Da apart, ratio ~3:1). Not seen. Bromine (79/81 ~2 Da, 1:1). Not seen. Sulfur (32,33,34,36) pattern includes +2 with ~4% intensity relative to monoisotopic. Here intensities: base peak at 233.9632 intensity 100. Adjacent +1 (232.9688) intensity 7.6, +2 (234.9666) intensity 9.8, +3 (235.9606) intensity 24.4, +4 (236.9639) intensity 2.37, +5 (237.9672) intensity 0.1. The pattern not typical for chlorine/bromine. The +1 is low (7.6%) suggests many carbons (13C distribution). The +2 is similar magnitude (9.8%). The +3 is higher (24%). This could be due to combination of 13C and 15N (mass difference 0.997). Also presence of 34S (2 Da) could increase +2. But we need elements that can be definitively identified from isotope pattern alone. Carbon is clear. Possibly sulfur if we see a distinct M+2 peak higher than expected from 13C alone? Hard to be definitive without formula. But we can retrieve isotopic distribution for elements to compare.
